Rashi on Arakhin 32a:10:1.hebrew: שגגותיה חומתה - שלא הקיפוה חומה, אלא הקיפוה בבתים, ותכופות הבתים זו לזו כחומה:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:10:1.english: Whose rooftops [are] its wall - [meaning] that they did not surround it with a wall, rather they surrounded it with houses, and the houses are adjacent to one another like a wall:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:10:2.hebrew: שלש חצירות - שבכל אחת ואחת שני בתים, מיקריא עיר:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:10:2.english: Three courtyards - [where] in each and every one [there are] two houses — [that] is called a city:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:10:3.english: Katzra - [The] name of a small town outside of Tzippori:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:11:1.english: A wall of roofs - [meaning] that its roofs are its wall:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:12:1.hebrew: לוא חומה - "לוא" כתיב, משמע "לא" ומשמע "לו", כלומר: אין לו עכשיו והיה לו חומה קודם, הוה נמי בית חלוט בהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:12:1.english: Lo a wall - It is written lo [spelled lamed-vav-alef], which implies "not" [lo] and implies "to it" [lo]; that is to say: [if] it does not have [a wall] now, and it had a wall previously, a house in them [i.e., such cities] also becomes permanently sold:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:13:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - וכי אין עיר מוקפת חומה בגליל אלא גמלא, ובעבר הירדן אלא גדוד:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:13:1.english: What is [he] saying - Is there really no walled city in the Galilee except Gamla, and in Transjordan except Gedod?

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:2:1.hebrew: שלא בפניו - כגון זה שהיה נטמן, ומשום דתרתי לריעותא איכא — דשלא בפניו הוא ובעל כרחו הוא — משום הכי איצטריך ליה להלל לתקוני:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:2:1.english: Not in his presence - For example, this [case] where [the buyer] was hiding; and because there are two disadvantages — that it is not in his presence and it is against his will — therefore it was necessary for Hillel to institute [this ordinance]:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:4:1.hebrew: מאי דאיצטריך ליה תקין - ואי הוי נמי לוקח התם, ולא הוה בעי לקבולינהו, הוה איצטריך להלל לתקוני דבעל כרחו תיהוי נתינה:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:4:1.english: [Hillel] instituted what was necessary - And even if the buyer were there and did not want to accept [the money], it would have been necessary for Hillel to institute [an ordinance] that against his will it should be [considered a valid] giving:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:6:1.english: House - [The verse states:] "Then the house that is in the city shall stand" (Leviticus 25:30):

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:6:2.english: Towers - Mostier [Old French for a monastery or church], and [it is] fixed in the ground:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:6:3.hebrew: ת"ל בית - והני דלעיל דמו לבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:6:3.english: The verse states: "House" - And these [items mentioned] above resemble a house:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:8:1.hebrew: חולסית - מקום שאינו ראוי לזריעה איכא בינייהו, דשדות ממש לא קאמר רבי מאיר, דהא "בית" כתיב ביה, אלא חולסית ומצולה קמרבי דדמו לבית, דלאו בני זריעה נינהו וראויין לבנין בית: חולסית ליטול משם אבנים, ומצולה ליטול מהן חול; ורבי יהודה סבר כשדות דמו:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:8:1.english: Cholsit - A place that is not fit for sowing is [the difference] between them; for Rabbi Meir did not mean actual fields, since "house" is written in [the verse], rather he includes cholsit and metzolah [because] they are similar to a house, in that they are not fit for sowing and are fit for building a house: cholsit [is a place] from which to take stones, and metzolah [is a place] from which to take sand; whereas Rabbi Yehudah holds [that] they are similar to fields.

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:8:2.english: And it is taught - [Read] calmly [i.e., as a statement rather than a question]:

Rashi on Arakhin 32a:9:1.hebrew: כפשטיה דקרא - דחזינן דביתה בתוך החומה, וקאמר "בחומה היא יושבת", כלומר: בעיר חומה היא יושבת:
Rashi on Arakhin 32a:9:1.english: In accordance with the simple meaning of the verse - for we see that her house was within the wall, and [the verse] states, "she dwelt upon the wall," meaning, she dwelt in a walled city:

Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:12:1.hebrew: אשר לו חומה - פירש רש"י: "לוא" כתיב, משמע "לו" ומשמע "לא", כלומר: אין לו עכשיו והיה לו קודם לכן. ואינו כן, בחומשין מדויקות כתיב [לא באל"ף, וקרי בוי"ו] (בוי"ו ולא קרי באל"ף):
Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:12:1.english: Which has [lo] a wall - Rashi explained: It is written לוא [with both a vav and an alef], which implies [both] לו ["has"] and לא ["does not have"], meaning: it does not have [a wall] now, but it had [one] previously. However, this is not so; in accurate Pentateuchs it is written [לא with an alef, and read with a vav] (with a vav, and not read with an alef):

Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:13:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - וכי אין עיר מוקפת חומה בגליל אלא גמלא, ובעבר הירדן אלא גדוד? ואם תאמר: אמאי לא פריך כמו כן אמתני'? ויש לומר: דפריך שפיר אברייתא, לפי שדקדקה יותר, דמפרשא בהדיא "גמלא בגליל וגדוד בעבר הירדן":
Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:13:1.english: What is [the tanna] saying - Is there really no walled city in the Galilee except Gamla, and in Transjordan except Gedod? And if you should ask: Why does [the Gemara] not raise the same difficulty against the Mishnah? One can answer that it properly raises the difficulty against the baraita, because [the baraita] was more exact, as it explicitly specifies: "Gamla is in the Galilee, and Gedod is in Transjordan":

Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:1:1.hebrew: מדאיצטריך הלל לתקוני נתינה בעל כרחו [הוי נתינה, הא בעלמא נתינה בע"כ] לא הויא נתינה - (פשיטא דאין לו לאדם לקבל מתנה בעל כרחו ולא הויא נתינה) וא"ת, וכי איצטריך ליה להביא ראיה על זה דנתינה בעל כרחו לא הויא נתינה? פשיטא דאין לו לאדם לקבל מתנה בעל כרחו! ועוד, היכי פליג על זה רב פפא? וי"ל, דודאי מתנה דרשות שאין לו שום צורך, פשיטא דלא הויא בעל כרחו, ורב פפא נמי לא פליג על זה; אלא במתנה שיש בה צורך פליגי, כמו הכא דאמר לה "זה גיטך ע"מ שתתן לי מאתים זוז", שהיא צריכה כדי לקיים תנאי הגט, וכגון קבלה דמתני'. [אבל] היכא דאיכא חובה לנותן, כגון חוב או פקדון, בהא ודאי הוי נתינה בעל כרחו, כדאיתא פרק הגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיח. ושם): הלוהו או שהפקיד אצלו בישוב, לא יחזיר לו במדבר — משמע הא בישוב מחזיר לו בעל כרחו. ואם תאמר: הא דתנן בפרק מי שאחזו (גיטין עד. ושם): "הרי זה גיטך על מנת שתתן לי איצטליתי", ואבדה איצטליתו, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר תתן דמיה — והתם מיירי אפי' בעל כרחו דבעל, מדפליגי רבנן עליה ואמרי "איצטליתו דוקא קאמר". תו בעי התם בגמרא: האומר לאשה "הרי זה גיטך ע"מ שתתני מאתים זוז", וחזר ואמר לה "מחולין לך", מהו? תיבעי לרבנן, תיבעי לרשב"ג. תיבעי לרבנן: עד כאן לא קא אמרי רבנן התם אלא היכא דלא אחליה לגבה, אבל הכא הא קאמר "מחולין לך". והא ע"כ דאמרי רבנן "איצטליתו דוקא קאמר", בעל כרחו מיירי, דאי מדעתו, לא גרע ממחולין לך; ואפ"ה קאמר רשב"ג "תתן לו דמיה", אלמא סבירא ליה לרשב"ג דנתינה בעל כרחו הויא נתינה. וא"כ, היכי קאמר רבא הכא דלא הויא נתינה? וצ"ל, דלרבא מיירי התם דאמר רשב"ג "תתן לו דמיה" מדעתיה קאמר, ואפילו הכי לרבנן איצטלית דוקא קאמר ואינה מגורשת, והאי בעיא דהתם אינה אליבא דרבא, דלרבא ודאי אליבא דרבנן אפילו "מחולין לך" לא מהני. ואם תאמר: לרבא דס"ל דאפילו בעיר לא הוי נתינה בע"כ, א"כ למה היה ללוקח להטמין? לימא "לא מקבלינא", ואז לא הוי נתינה והחליט לו אחר י"ב חדשים! וי"ל, דאם היה בעיר, היה בוש ממנו אם לא היה מקבל. וא"ת: משמע דלרבא אפילו בפניו בע"כ לא הויא נתינה; והיכי מצי להוכיח מהכא בפניו? והלא תקנת הלל לא היתה כי אם שלא בפניו, וכי איצטריך ליה להלל לתקוני שלא בפניו, אבל בפניו, בין מדעתו בין בעל כרחו הוי נתינה, כדמתקיף ליה רב פפא! וי"ל דמוכח הכי: דאם איתא דבפניו הוי נתינה בעל כרחו, לא הוה צריך להילל לתקוני שלא בפניו להיות חולש מעותיו ללשכה, דהא אפשר לזכות לו ע"י אחר; אלא שמע מינה מדאיצטריך ליה להלל לתקן נתינה בעל כרחו, הא בעלמא כו'. ורב פפא דאתקיף ליה לית ליה האי סברא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:1:1.english: Since Hillel needed to institute [that] giving against [the recipient's] will [is considered giving, one may infer that in general, giving against one's will] is not [considered] giving - (It is obvious that a person need not accept a gift against his will, and it is not [considered] giving.) And if you ask: Did [the Gemara] need to bring a proof for this, that giving against [one's] will is not [considered] giving? It is obvious that a person need not accept a gift against his will! Furthermore, how does Rav Pappa disagree with this? And one can answer: Certainly, [regarding] a discretionary gift where [the recipient] has no need [for it], it is obvious that it is not [valid] against his will, and Rav Pappa also does not disagree with this. Rather, they disagree regarding a gift in which [one] has a need, such as here, where [a husband] says to her, "This is your bill of divorce on condition that you give me two hundred zuz," where she needs [to do so] in order to fulfill the condition of the bill of divorce, and similarly the acceptance in our Mishnah. [However,] where there is an obligation upon the giver, such as a debt or a deposit, in that case it is certainly [considered] giving against [the recipient's] will, as it is stated in the chapter [entitled] HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 118a and there): [If] one lent to him or deposited with him in a settled area, he may not return [it] to him in the wilderness — this implies that in a settled area he may return [it] to him against his will. And if you ask: [Regarding] that which we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (Gittin 74a and there): "This is your bill of divorce on condition that you give me my cloak," and his cloak was lost — Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: She shall give its value. And there it is speaking even against the husband's will, from the fact that the Rabbis disagree with him and say, "He meant his cloak specifically." Furthermore, [the Gemara] asks there in the Gemara: [Regarding] one who says to a woman, "This is your bill of divorce on condition that you give [me] two hundred zuz," and he went back and said to her, "They are forgiven to you," what is [the law]? Let it be asked according to the Rabbis, [and] let it be asked according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Let it be asked according to the Rabbis: Thus far the Rabbis only said [that she is not divorced] there where he did not forgive it to her, but here he said, "They are forgiven to you." Now, perforce, when the Rabbis say "he meant his cloak specifically," it is speaking [of a case] against his will — for if [it were] with his consent, it would be no worse than "they are forgiven to you"; and even so, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, "She shall give him its value"! Thus, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that giving against [the recipient's] will is [considered] giving. And if so, how does Rava say here that it is not [considered] giving? And one must say that according to Rava, [the Mishnah] there, where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says "she shall give him its value," is speaking [of a case where] he says [so] with his consent; and even so, according to the Rabbis, he meant a cloak specifically and she is not divorced. And that question there is not according to Rava, for according to Rava, certainly according to the Rabbis even "they are forgiven to you" is of no avail. And if you ask: According to Rava, who holds that even in the city it is not [considered] giving against [the buyer's] will, if so, why did the buyer have to hide? Let him say, "I do not accept [it]," and then it would not be [considered] giving, and [the house] would be permanently his after twelve months! And one can answer that if he were in the city, he would be embarrassed before him if he did not accept [it]. And if you ask: It implies that according to Rava, even in his presence against his will it is not [considered] giving; and how can [Rava] prove from here [the case of] in his presence? Was Hillel's enactment not only [for] not in his presence, and Hillel only needed to institute [it] for not in his presence, whereas in his presence, whether with his consent or against his will, it is [considered] giving — as Rav Pappa objects to him! And one can answer that it is proven thus: for if it were true that in his presence it is [considered] giving against his will, Hillel would not have needed to institute [anything] for not in his presence, to deposit his money in the [Temple] chamber, since it is possible to acquire [it] for him through another [person]; rather, learn from this [that] since Hillel needed to institute giving against [the recipient's] will, in general, etc. And Rav Pappa, who objects to him, does not hold this reasoning:

Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:8:1.hebrew: חולסית - פירש"י: ליטול משם אבנים, ומצולה — ליטול משם חול. ורשב"ם פירש בב"ב (דף סז. ושם): חולסית — ליטול הימנה זכוכית, ומצולה — כמו (ברכות דף ט:) "מצולה של דגים":
Tosafot on Arakhin 32a:8:1.english: Ḥolsit - Rashi explained: [a place from which] to take stones, and metzolah — [a place from which] to take sand. And Rashbam explained in Bava Batra (67a, and there): ḥolsit — [a place from which] to take [sand for] glass, and metzolah — like (Berakhot 9b) "a depth of fish":
